messages:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock acceptance criteria for the VPC/on‑prem packaging handshakes this sprint. Customers are asking for clear fallback windows and upgrade contracts. Can we list the must-have gates by EOD?

Ajay Sinha: +1. Major asks from NetOps: preserve customer IPs, deterministic peering teardown, and a clear rollback path. Also need a required-min-version for the agent.

Sophie Kim: For rollout: propose these gates — (1) successful canary in staging with 2 customers, (2) automated e2e connection test (BGP peering + mTLS) green, (3) zero-data-loss handshake test (migration with traffic mirroring).

Kevin Wu: Dovetailing on Sophie — define acceptable downtime window. Customers expect <5m for control-plane switch, but some expect no interruption. We should call out two tiers: "non-disruptive" (preferred) and "allowed short window" (fallback).

Maria Chen: Good. Draft acceptance checklist I'm thinking:
- Agent compatibility pinned (min 1.4.0)
- Handshake: seq-numbered config apply + automatic rollback on health-check fail
- Network: preserved source IPs OR documented SNAT behavior for customers that accept it
- Security: customer KMS integration for keys, audit logs exported to their SIEM
- Observability: per-route latency and error budget on the console
- Rollout: staged canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallbacks

Ajay Sinha: Can we add a specific test for IP preservation? E.g.: run `curl --resolve` style flow from customer subnet and assert original src shows up in logs. Put that in the e2e checklist.

Sophie Kim: Adding: test matrix for NAT vs no-NAT paths. Also confirm whether edge connector requires iptables or supports eBPF forwarding (contrast for on‑prem kernel versions).

Kevin Wu: Ops constraints: support kernel >=5.4 for eBPF path; otherwise fall back to iptables. Note in docs and acceptance criteria: if customer kernel <5.4, we ship with iptables mode but mark as "best-effort" for perf SLA.

Maria Chen: @Sophie, @Ajay — owner mapping? I propose: Ajay owns network test definitions, Sophie owns rollout playbook + docs, Kevin owns compatibility matrix and perf SLAs. I'll own stakeholder comms and launch gate approval.

Ajay Sinha: Ack. I'll drop a short test harness snippet into the repo by tomorrow. Prototype command: 
```
# run preserved-ip test
./ci/e2e --customer-subnet 10.2.0.0/24 --assert-src-ip=10.2.0.5
```
I'll also add a teardown test that simulates peering failover and validates automatic rollback.

Sophie Kim: I'll draft the staged rollout runbook and include playbook steps for manual rollback and automated fallback hooks. Will include the canary acceptance signal (error rate <0.5% and latency P95 delta <20ms).

Kevin Wu: I'll publish compatibility doc with kernel, Docker, and agent version matrices. Also will add a short benchmark showing eBPF vs iptables perf to justify recommended default.

deploy-bot: Deploy preview created for branch `pkg/handshake/gates` — preview URL: https://staging.redwood.dev/previews/handshake-2290 (tests queued) :rocket:

Maria Chen: Nice — can we set a hard acceptance cutoff on Friday EOD? If we don't meet the two canary customers criteria by then, we move to soft-launch with additional guardrails.

Ajay Sinha: Friday EOD works. I'll prioritize the preserved-IP and teardown tests.

Sophie Kim: Same — will have runbook draft + checklist by Thursday lunchtime.

Kevin Wu: Compatibility matrix by Thursday EOD.

Maria Chen: Ok team — action items summarized: Ajay = network tests; Sophie = rollout + runbook; Kevin = compatibility + perf; Maria = launch comms & gate decision. Will follow up with stakeholder summary doc. :thumbsup:

Ajay Sinha: noted. tagging @network-eng for visibility. :eyes:

Sophie Kim: Thanks — adding a note to the product board with the acceptance checklist and links.

Kevin Wu: Ping me if you need me to run perf runs on dedicated infra.

Maria Chen: Great. Closing this thread — will reopen if gating criteria change.
